title: Blind Charlie and Steve Lewis, piano players
summary: He recalls Blanc Charlie playing blues piano, bass and banjo, and Steve Lewis as the best floor-show pianist who needed to learn music, with some remarks on pay.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: You know. What about Blonde Charlie? Don't interrupt him. Don't interrupt him. Don't interrupt him. Tell him. and different things like that. Every time we used a good chord, we were right time music then. We didn't know nothing about jazz, you know. Every time we used a good chord, right time music then. What about Blanc Charlie? Steve Lewis, he could play. What about Blanc Charlie?

Blanc Charlie was a good blue piano too. He played piano, bass, and banditore, Blanc Charlie. Banditore too. He was just a blue playing piano, you know. He could make out his band, put a fuzz, and be a blind man, you know.
It's best not to interrupt him. Don't interrupt him. You know, when he gets started on something like Steve Lewis, ask him what he was going to say about Steve.

He said, what you going to say about Steve? Steve, do you play with me? I play by myself. He said, you know, ask my cornet and jambore to play. He said, you know, just sing and holler, you know, like that. He's got Sammy D'Angie or something like that. Sammy D'Angie. I've used to say he could read there, because he wouldn't have been with Piranha if he couldn't read. No, that's a good one. I don't know.
Some fella like, you like that day? I was the one called out there, he knew the day, after

he had a good year. And he was the best flow show piano player I had there in the city. And when I was getting on them jobs with my sister, they said, well, I'll tell you he didn't know about it, and he'd get out there because he was a good speaker, you know. Well, they'd keep him a while, they'd break that job out, but they wouldn't keep. So I said, I tell you, why don't you learn music now? I said, that's a good man. He said, you get by. He did what I said. He just stayed on music now about three, four years. He said, he had that job down there about nine years. Everybody's good. He don't do no job, letting the people go broke or something like that. Just since I've been sick, I haven't been able to go. He always tell me, he said, Mom, as long as you ain't doing nothing, he said, I want you to be right with me. He said, to help me to have some fun off the money I throw away. I said, it's the time, you know. And he said, so changing my way all the time, you know. But I got out to Union, you know, and then after they got back on guitar, I didn't want to take all that time, you know. They shouldn't come up to getting too bad around there and then, and them inches, I've been going up, you see. Up there, $200, $250 for that band, I got there. Now it costs more than that, now. Who is Sammy DeAnzey asking about that? He knows.
